key_insight: Privacy-preserving knowledge distillation can transfer LLM-based multimorbidity reasoning into compact models without using real patient data, while preserving strong predictive performance.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support safer, scalable multimorbidity scoring in health systems by improving survival prediction from biobank-scale data.
method: Trained student CoLLMs by distilling knowledge from LLM teacher models
Used synthetic cohorts designed to match UK Biobank distributions
Evaluated transfer quality and downstream performance on real UK Biobank data
evidence_signal: Distillation showed high-fidelity transfer (Spearman rho 0.75-0.89), and CoLLM scores improved survival prediction (C-index up to 0.91) with higher SNP heritability (h2 ~0.05).
watch_item: Results depend on synthetic-cohort realism and teacher-model choice, and the approach still needs careful validation before broad deployment.
paper_title: Privacy-Aware Distillation of Large Language Models for Enhanced Multimorbidity Scoring
